C.2 Time-reversal symmetry

Akin to the U(1) case, one can employ Eqs. (102)–(106) to determine the ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} PSG associated with time-reversal symmetry. On substituting Eq. (228) into Eqs. (103) and (104), we obtain

W𝒯​(x,y,u)=η𝒯​xx​η𝒯​yy​W𝒯,u.\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}}(x,y,u)=\eta_{\mathcal{T}x}^{x}\eta_{\mathcal{T}y}^{y}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},u}. (258)

Next, inserting the solutions given by Eqs. (231), (234), and (258) into Eqs. (102), (105), and (106), we arrive at the following constraints:

W𝒯,u2\displaystyle W_{\mathcal{T},u}^{2} =η𝒯​τ0,\displaystyle=\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}}\tau^{0}, (259)
W𝒯,u​WC2,u​W𝒯,u¯−1​WC2,u−1\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},u}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2},u}W_{\mathcal{T},\bar{u}}^{-1}W_{C_{2},u}^{-1} =η𝒯​C2​τ0,\displaystyle=\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}C_{2}}\tau^{0}\,, (260)
η𝒯​x\displaystyle\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}x} =1,\displaystyle=1, (261)
W𝒯,u​Wσx,u​W𝒯,u¯−1​Wσx,u−1\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},u}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x},u}W_{\mathcal{T},\bar{u}}^{-1}W_{\sigma_{x},u}^{-1} =η𝒯​σx​τ0.\displaystyle=\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}\sigma_{x}}\tau^{0}\,. (262)

From Eqs. (251) and (262), one deduces that

W𝒯,2=η𝒯​σx​W𝒯,1.\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},2}=\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}\sigma_{x}}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},1}. (263)

Combining this with Eq. (259) leads to

η𝒯=+1:W𝒯,u={1,η𝒯​σx}​τ0,\displaystyle\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}}=+1:\quad W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},u}=\{1,\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}\sigma_{x}}\}\tau^{0}, (264)
η𝒯=−1:W𝒯,u={1,η𝒯​σx}​ι˙​𝒗^⋅τ^,\displaystyle\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}}=-1:\quad W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T},u}=\{1,\eta^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}\sigma_{x}}\}\,\dot{\iota}\,\bm{\hat{v}}\cdot\mathbf{\hat{\tau}}, (265)

where 𝒗^∈ℝ3\bm{\hat{v}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3} is a unit vector. Importantly, the case η𝒯​σx=+1\eta_{\mathcal{T}\sigma_{x}}=+1 with η𝒯=+1\eta_{\mathcal{T}}=+1 does not yield a PSG compatible with nonvanishing mean-field amplitudes, and is therefore excluded from the classification. The remaining ambiguity associated with 𝒗^\bm{\hat{v}} is resolved through the constraint in Eq. (260). All gauge-inequivalent solutions, including those derived here, are summarized in Table 2.

Appendix D Construction of mean-field Ansätze

Having obtained all projective realizations of the space-group symmetry elements, one can construct lattice-symmetric mean-field Ansätze using the condition

W𝒪†​(𝒪⁡(i))​u𝒪⁡(i)​𝒪​(j)​W𝒪​(𝒪⁡(j))=ui​j.W^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{O}(i))\,u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{O}(i)\mathcal{O}(j)}\,W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{O}(j))=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}. (266)

For a composite symmetry operator 𝒪3=𝒪2​𝒪1\mathcal{O}_{3}=\mathcal{O}_{2}\mathcal{O}_{1}, this condition becomes

W𝒪1†​(𝒪1​(i))\displaystyle W^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{O}_{1}}(\mathcal{O}_{1}(i))\, W𝒪2†​(𝒪3​(i))\displaystyle W^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{O}_{2}}(\mathcal{O}_{3}(i))\, u𝒪3​(i)​𝒪3​(j)\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{O}_{3}(i)\mathcal{O}_{3}(j)}
×\displaystyle\times W𝒪2​(𝒪3​(j))​W𝒪1​(𝒪1​(j))=ui​j.\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{O}_{2}}(\mathcal{O}_{3}(j))\,W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{O}_{1}}(\mathcal{O}_{1}(j))=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}. (267)

Analogous conditions can be derived for any Ansatz involving longer strings of symmetry operations.

We define symmetry-allowed mean-field parameters on representative bonds within a unit cell. The corresponding parameters on all other bonds are generated via translations:

On JvJ_{v} bonds: u(0,0,1),(0,0,2)=uv,\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{(0,0,1),(0,0,2)}=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}, (268)
On JhJ_{h} bonds: u(0,0,1),(1,0,1)=uh,\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{(0,0,1),(1,0,1)}=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{h}, (269)
u(0,0,2),(1,0,2)=uh′,\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{(0,0,2),(1,0,2)}=u^{\prime}_{h}, (270)
On JzJ_{z} bonds: u(0,0,1),(0,1,2)=uz,\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{(0,0,1),(0,1,2)}=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{z}, (271)
u(0,0,1),(−1,1,2)=uz′.\displaystyle u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{(0,0,1),(-1,1,2)}=u_{z}^{\prime}. (272)

A symmetry operation 𝒪\mathcal{O} can affect a link field ui​ju^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij} in one of three ways:

  1. 1.

    Leave it invariant: 𝒪:ui​j→ui​j\mathcal{O}:u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}\rightarrow u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}.

  2. 2.

    Reverse its direction: 𝒪:ui​j→uj​i=ui​j†\mathcal{O}:u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}\rightarrow u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ji}=u^{\dagger}_{ij}.

  3. 3.

    Map it to a different, symmetry-equivalent link: 𝒪:ui​j→ui′​j′\mathcal{O}:u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}\rightarrow u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{i^{\prime}j^{\prime}}, with ⟨i′​j′⟩≠⟨i​j⟩\langle i^{\prime}j^{\prime}\rangle\neq\langle ij\rangle.

The first two scenarios determine symmetry-allowed mean-field parameters, while the third relates distinct but symmetry-equivalent bonds across the lattice.

The conditions relevant for our classification are

σx:\displaystyle\sigma^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{x}: uv→uv†,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}\rightarrow u_{v}^{\dagger}, (273)
C2:\displaystyle C^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}: uv→uv†,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}\rightarrow u_{v}^{\dagger}, (274)
C2​σx:\displaystyle C^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}\sigma_{x}: uv→uv,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}\rightarrow u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}, (275)
T1​C2​σx:\displaystyle T^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{1}C^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}\sigma_{x}: uh→uh†,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{h}\rightarrow u_{h}^{\dagger}, (276)
σx:\displaystyle\sigma^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{x}: uh→uh′,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{h}\rightarrow u^{\prime}_{h}, (277)
T2​C2:\displaystyle T^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}C^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}: uz→uz†,\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{z}\rightarrow u_{z}^{\dagger}, (278)
σx​C2:\displaystyle\sigma^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{x}C^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{2}: uz→uz′.\displaystyle\quad u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{z}\rightarrow u^{\prime}_{z}. (279)

The corresponding projective symmetry conditions read:

Wσx†​(0,0,2)​uv†​Wσx​(0,0,1)\displaystyle W_{\sigma_{x}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)u_{v}^{\dagger}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x}}(0,0,1) =uv,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}, (280)
WC2†​(0,0,2)​uv†​WC2​(0,0,1)\displaystyle W_{C_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)u_{v}^{\dagger}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2}}(0,0,1) =uv,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}, (281)
Wσx†​(0,0,2)​WC2†​(0,0,1)​uv​WC2​(0,0,2)\displaystyle W_{\sigma_{x}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)W_{C_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,0,1)u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2}}(0,0,2)
Wσx​(0,0,1)\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x}}(0,0,1) =uv,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{v}, (282)
Wσx†​(0,0,2)​WC2†​(0,0,1)​WT1†​(1,0,1)​uh†\displaystyle W_{\sigma_{x}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)W_{C_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,0,1)W_{T_{1}}^{\dagger}(1,0,1)u_{h}^{\dagger}
WT1​(0,0,1)​WC2​(−1,0,1)​Wσx​(1,0,2)\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{T_{1}}(0,0,1)W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2}}(-1,0,1)W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x}}(1,0,2) =uh,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{h}, (283)
Wσx†​(0,0,2)​uh′​Wσx​(1,0,2)\displaystyle W_{\sigma_{x}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)u^{\prime}_{h}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x}}(1,0,2) =uh,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{h}, (284)
WC2†​(0,0,2)​WT2†​(0,1,2)​uz†​WT2​(0,0,1)\displaystyle W_{C_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)W_{T_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,1,2)u_{z}^{\dagger}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{T_{2}}(0,0,1)
WC2​(0,−1,1)\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2}}(0,-1,1) =uz,\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{z}, (285)
WC2†​(0,0,2)​Wσx†​(0,0,1)​uz′​Wσx​(−1,1,2)\displaystyle W_{C_{2}}^{\dagger}(0,0,2)W_{\sigma_{x}}^{\dagger}(0,0,1)u^{\prime}_{z}W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\sigma_{x}}(-1,1,2)
WC2​(0,−1,1)\displaystyle W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{C_{2}}(0,-1,1) =uz.\displaystyle=u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{z}\,. (286)

Additionally, time-reversal invariance dictates that

W𝒯†​(i)​ui​j​W𝒯​(j)=−ui​j.W_{\mathcal{T}}^{\dagger}(i)\,u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}\,W^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{\mathcal{T}}(j)=-u^{\phantom{\dagger}}_{ij}. (287)

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
